thread:
Alex (infra): FYI - vendor sent an updated EDP draft. there's a weird 'shock' clause that converts unused committed GPUs into non-refundable credits if availability falls below 95% for >7 days. wondering if anyone has seen this and thoughts on counters. :thinking:
Sam (vendor): Hey all — that's our cloud partner's standard ops protection. It protects their allocation planning. We asked for a carveout but they pushed back. We can ask them to tie it to region-level SLA instead of global aggregate.
Maya (finance): Can you paste the exact wording? need to run high-level $ impact if that clause triggers.
Alex (infra): Pasting relevant excerpt:```
"If Provider is unable to deliver >= 95% of contracted GPU capacity for any contiguous 7-day period due to capacity constraints, Redwood Inference agrees to convert up to 50% of unused committed value into non-refundable credits for Provider-managed services, applied within 90 days."```
Ritu (legal): That's aggressive. Two immediate asks: 1) define "unable to deliver" (is it preemption events? scheduled maintenance?) 2) add cure period + remediation obligations (e.g., provider must propose remediation plan within 48h). Also push to convert credits to term extension rather than cash-forfeit.
Chris (ops): Practical ops note: We frequently burst cross-region during peak training. If they measure per-region strictness we might trip this even if global capacity is fine. Ask them to permit cross-region substitution (same cloud family + network egress neutral).
Sam (vendor): Noted. Their initial reply: they measure per-region and per-SKU. They said cross-region substitution requires prior notice and maybe a migration window. I'll ask for auto-failover allowance for inter-region substitution for first 12 months.
Maya (finance): Quick back-of-envelope: if we commit 120 A100s reserved at $2.5M/yr and 50% converted to credits, that's $1.25M lost value we can't reallocate. We need either refundable credits or the ability to apply credits to other SKUs/services. Also insist on quarterly true-up, not annual.
Alex (infra): Also pushing for a burst buffer: allow 10% temporary overcommit per month with no penalty if we pay on-demand rates for the extra. That prevents false positives during spikes.
Ritu (legal): Draft alternative clause suggestion below — propose this to provider:```
"Provider shall be deemed to have failed delivery only where Provider cannot provide capacity across eligible regions (us-east1, us-west2, europe-west1) for a contiguous 7-day window, after Provider has exhausted automated failover and substitution options. Provider shall notify Redwood within 4 hours of threshold breach and have 72 hours to remediate. Any conversion to credits shall be optional and may be applied as a term-extension or transferable service credit. Redwood retains audit right to verify capacity metrics within a 12-month window."```
Sam (vendor): I can push that. They are likely to accept region-grouping and remediation windows; transferability is harder but worth asking.
Chris (ops): Two more ops asks: 1) define measurement granularity (per-hour median? p95?) we want p95 across 24h windows, not instantaneous. 2) credit calculation should be based on unused GPU-hours not flat contracted $ to avoid over-penalizing short blips.
Maya (finance): Agreed. Also add explicit carveout for force majeure and cloud-side migrations (like when provider performs capacity reshuffle) — shouldn't trigger conversion.
Alex (infra): Also flagged: meter reconciliation cadence. We need detailed daily metering report and an API hook. If meter lag >30 days, no penalty can be enforced until reconciliation complete.
Sam (vendor): Vendor response: they'll consider p95 and hourly aggregation, but will want longer audit window on our side (18 months). They asked for an automated monthly report from us if we want migratory credits.
Ritu (legal): We can accept 18 months but cap their ability to retroactively charge credits to 12 months after an explicit true-up. Also propose an escrowed mitigation fund (small monthly buffer) that provider can draw from while remediating; funds refundable if SLA met.
Maya (finance): If we do an escrow, suggest 2% of committed annual spend as buffer, refundable quarterly. That reduces one-time risk. Run numbers vs price concession.
Alex (infra): Ops-lifecycle ask: require a fallback-policy in console to auto-route requests to compatible model variants / cross-region pool before counting as lost capacity. This should be visible in their audit logs.
Sam (vendor): I'll collate asks: region-grouping, p95 hourly measurement, 72h remediation, credits -> term-extension/transferability, daily meter API, escrow option 2% refundable, cross-region auto-failover acceptance for 12 months. I'll push in the call tomorrow.
Chris (ops): Also ask for a clause allowing SKU substitution (e.g., if A100 not available, equivalent TFLOPS GPU in same family is acceptable) with <=5% performance variance allowed.
Maya (finance): Next step: Sam please get their initial thumbs-up/no on each bullet before legal drafts redline. I'll model the 2% escrow vs 5% price concession trade.
Ritu (legal): I'll prepare a redline of the EDP with the alt clause and escrow language that preserves audit and remediation.
Alex (infra): Great. If vendor pushes back on transferability, accept term-extension + ability to use credits for network/storage for limited services, but not permanently locked.
Sam (vendor): Understood. I'll push and share their reply in this thread. Meeting scheduled 2026-05-11 10:00 PT with vendor procurement. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Reminder: "vendor-call-2026-05-11" created and calendar invite sent to participants.
Maya (finance): Thanks — prepping high-level scenarios. Will post the spreadsheet link when ready. :+1:
Alex (infra): Thanks everyone. If anything else to add, drop here before EOD today.
